target_journal: The European Journal on Artificial Intelligence

outcome.scalar_progress_definition: Signed normalised potential gain over H steps: (phi(s_t+H) - phi(s_t)) / phi_ref, where phi is the potential (larger is better) and phi_ref is the median potential at the first decision point of the pilot. No zero floor: negative values are allowed and mean worse than the factual arm.
outcome.progress_ref: median potential at first decision point over pilot episodes
outcome.progress_note: The [0,1] floor of v1.0 collapsed every inferior arm to 0, made Delta indistinguishable, degraded DAR to a five-way classification and dropped the Gate-2 chance level from 0.50 to 0.20; v1.1 made the quantity signed. Gate-0's potential phi is still not clipped, so the two are different quantities.
outcome.horizon_note: From v1.3 the primary horizon is H=6, because the decision unit is a plan of length plan_len=3: the plan runs 3 steps and only the remaining 3 separate closed loop (frozen-policy replanning) from open loop (replaying the factual actions). If plan_len == H the two conventions coincide and the C/O gap -- itself a reported result -- becomes the constant 0.

candidate_set.rule_selection: Select by the rule table of Section 5: continuous actions -> R-samp; discrete or logits -> R-top. The v1.0/v1.1 implementations wrongly used R-top on continuous 3-dimensional incremental actions.
candidate_set.dedup: A candidate whose largest component difference from arm0 or from another candidate is below min_arm_sep counts as a duplicate and is redrawn deterministically; if no candidate can be drawn, raise rather than silently keeping a duplicate.
candidate_set.unit_note: From v1.3 the elements of the candidate set are plans rather than single actions; see decision_unit.

degenerate.definition: The final states of the K arms coincide within the eps tolerance at the end of the H steps, or all Y^(k) == Y^(0).

metrics.diagnosis_truth_construction: Per-variable from-I-to-s interventions back to ground truth; a variable that can be rescued this way is the offending one.

leakage_assertions: no test scene instance in train
no test task template in train

Gate-1_intervention_locality.test: After intervening on edge e, the predictions of non-adjacent nodes change by less than 1% of that node's natural fluctuation.
Gate-1_intervention_locality.on_fail: fix the model, not the metric

uniform_random.DAR_measurement: Permute the ground truth B=200 times and report the mean and standard deviation of DAR.
uniform_random.permute_what: y_true (not y_pred): shuffling y_pred degenerates to the identity map on an uninformative baseline.
uniform_random.forbidden_analytic_shortcut: p^2+(1-p)^2 ignores the correlation induced by the shared within-row baseline: it measures 0.917 where permutation gives 0.493, so it must not be used.
uniform_random.note: The criterion is that an uninformative predictor must not score high (<0.75), not that it must equal 0.5; report p_positive alongside, because when p approaches 0 or 1 the table does not support a directional metric.

Gate-2_ruler_self_test.on_fail: the metric is biased: fix the metric before running experiments

change_control.any_violation: rerun every main experiment; earlier results are void

changelog.change: Y_prog made signed; the Gate-2 chance level computed from the data as p^2+(1-p)^2; ruler_selftest permutes y_true rather than y_pred
changelog.reason: Pilot measurement: the zero floor collapsed every inferior arm's Y to 0, made Delta indistinguishable, degraded DAR to a five-way classification and put the chance level at 0.20 rather than 0.50; shuffling y_pred is silently misused on an uninformative baseline.
changelog.main_experiments_rerun: none (pilot stage, main experiments had not started)

changelog.change: the decision unit changed from a single action to a plan of length 3; the primary horizon moved from H=3 to H=6; the candidate perturbation became a mixture of a persistent bias and a per-step alternating term; R-top is disabled when plan_len>1
changelog.reason: Measured horizon collapse at v1.2 (rank correlation 0.905, 73.9% of decisions fully co-ordered, argmax agreement 88.1%, and widening the dispersion did not help): at H=3 the horizon is decoration and the DAR gain cannot support a claim about multi-step reasoning.
changelog.main_experiments_rerun: none (still pilot stage, main experiments had not started)

code_contract.mismatched_version_results: must not enter a paper table

control_cadence.note: v1.1 and earlier implemented 5 substeps (100 Hz), so H=3 covered only 30 ms and counterfactual differences accounted for 0.6% of the between-step variance of Y; 10 Hz is the standard cadence for policy-level decisions.
control_cadence.horizon_note: From v1.3 horizon_s is computed from primary_horizon (6 x 0.1 s = 0.6 s) instead of being written independently: H changing while horizon_s stayed put is exactly the drift v1.2 left behind.

decision_unit.factual_plan_definition: the action sequence obtained by running the frozen base policy for plan_len consecutive steps from the state at the decision time
decision_unit.alternative_proposal: eps_h = k * [(1 - alt_frac) b + alt_frac (-1)^h q]，b/q ~ N(0, sigma^2)^3，k = 1/sqrt((1-alt_frac)^2 + alt_frac^2)，plan_h = clip(fact_h + eps_h, -1, 1)
decision_unit.persistent_term: b: a bias shared by the whole plan (with it alone, the plan is equivalent to the first action scaled by plan_len)
decision_unit.alternating_term: (-1)^h * q: alternates per step, so that 'left then right' and 'right then left' are distinguishable
decision_unit.dedup: Require both max|delta_a| >= min_arm_sep and mean|delta_a| >= min_spread, redrawing deterministically; if no candidate can be drawn, raise rather than silently keeping a duplicate.
decision_unit.rule_forbidden_reason: R-top picks candidates by their one-step myopic score; on a plan unit this welds a one-step oracle into the data generation and makes the question under test -- can one-step information rank plans -- unanswerable.
decision_unit.why: Measured horizon collapse of the single-action unit at v1.2: rank correlation 0.905 between the 1-step and H-step orderings, 73.9% fully co-ordered, argmax agreement 88.1%, and widening the dispersion did not help (0.92-0.94). A plan unit makes each later action act on the state the previous action produced, so H=1 information cannot rank plans by construction.
decision_unit.dispersion_normalisation: k is set so that the marginal standard deviation of the per-step perturbation is always proposal_sigma=0.8, independent of alt_frac and plan_len. Without the normalisation the raw mixture has marginal std 0.707*sigma at alt_frac=0.5, m=1 candidates would be more concentrated than m=3 ones, and 'm=1 collapses, m=3 does not' would acquire a dispersion explanation unrelated to the plan unit.
decision_unit.lag1_correlation_identity: corr(eps_h, eps_{h+1}) = ((1-w)^2 - w^2) / ((1-w)^2 + w^2); zero at w=0.5, +1 at w=0 (a pure persistent bias, i.e. a single action scaled by m), -1 at w=1
